title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked, LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the incremental detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared model family "gpt-5-mini" and a deterministic task generator, we collected Npairs = 720 complete paired episodes. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation and an allowed single repair stage) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, artifact-grounded counts and inference, a concise methods clarification clarifying provider-call auditing and the apparent audit asymmetry, an artifact-grounded interpretation that attributes the near-zero marginal effect to validator ceiling and curated input selection, and reproducibility guidance pointing to the archived execution manifest and canonical artifact bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being adopted to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational assurance requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and policy invariants. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and tool reports document this architectural trend and motivate empirical, workflow‑centred evaluations [1]–[3]. However, large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added specifically by an automated sandboxed-execution stage—when the same generated candidate is examined by both comparator conditions—remain scarce. We preregistered and executed a controlled paired study to quantify that marginal detection contribution under shared_initial_candidate semantics and to surface boundary conditions for when sandboxed emulation is operationally valuable.
sections.related_work: Recent survey and systems work position generate→validate→repair (and, where feasible, sandboxed emulation) as practical mitigations to raise trustworthiness for intent→configuration pipelines [1], [2]. Research in program and specification verification shows verification-guided repair improves correctness in adjacent domains [4], and prototype NetOps systems demonstrate mixed gains from emulator-assisted validation: emulation can show temporal or stateful failures that rule-based validators omit, but the incremental yield depends on validator coverage and input diversity [2], [3], [5]. These studies motivate a paired experimental design that isolates downstream guarded-stage signals by reusing the identical initial generated candidate across the compared pipelines, thereby attributing any between-condition discordance to validation/emulation/repair stages rather than to generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Study design and preregistration. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The design targeted Npairs = 720 with a preregistered minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning and specified deterministic inclusion/exclusion, missingness handling, multiplicity treatment for exploratory comparisons, and contamination controls.

Task bank, topology templates, and vendor abstraction. Confirmatory items were produced deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 generator. The bank covers three abstract vendor‑CLI families and three small topology templates (leaf–spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest explicitly encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make‑before‑break). Inclusion required vendor‑parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory run.

Model and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded in the execution manifest). For each task we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate and that identical candidate was analyzed under both the baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). This isolates any between-condition discordance to downstream guarded-stage observations or permitted repair activity.

Baseline validator. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based engine applying vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks versus required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change), protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance tests. The validator emits a binary detection flag and a validator_trace object documenting parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation codes.

Guarded pipeline and sandboxed emulation. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then, irrespective of validator outcome, executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and replays normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulation maps runtime observations (interface admin transitions and concurrency, MTU/VLAN applications, observable reachability changes) into runtime-observation rules that can trigger a detection not encoded in the static validator’s rule set. The emulation-to-detection mapping is intentionally conservative.

Repair policy and provider-call accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task and only in the guarded condition after emulation observations were available. The confirmatory provider-call audit records model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. To make audit fields transparent, we explicitly clarify provider-call audit semantics below.

Provider‑call audit: meaning of stage_counts and condition_counts. The execution manifest contains a provider_call_audit object with two orthogonal summaries: (a) stage_counts enumerates the number of provider-call events per execution stage (for example, shared_initial_generation and repair), and (b) condition_counts tallies provider-call events associated with logical pipeline phases under the shared_initial_candidate protocol. Under our preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics a single initial-generation provider call (shared_initial_generation) is produced per pair and is presented to both downstream conditions; those calls are therefore counted under stage_counts as shared_initial_generation = 720 and under condition_counts as the key labeled "shared" = 720 to indicate they were shared between baseline and guarded analyses. Repair-stage calls—invoked only by the guarded execution after emulation results—are counted under stage_counts as repair = 1 and under condition_counts as the key labeled "guarded" = 1 because they occurred only in the guarded pipeline. This orthogonality explains the apparent asymmetry in condition_counts while preserving complete_pair_count = 720: the asymmetry reflects event-type differences (shared initial generation versus guarded-only repair) rather than missing or unequal paired episodes.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis used a paired-binary procedure (McNemar/paired logistic style) to compute the aggregate paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline). We report exact McNemar two-sided p and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and contamination were handled per the preregistration; in this run complete_pair_count = 720 and failed_episode_count = 0, so primary inference used the full paired set.
sections.results:
Primary paired counts and inference (artifact-grounded). The confirmatory contingency counts are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All reported numeric values are verbatim outputs from the preregistered analysis executor.

Discordant‑pair attribution and repair accounting. Provider-call auditing shows stage_counts with a single repair event and condition_counts that reflect 720 shared initial-generation events and one guarded-only repair event. Because the same sampled candidate was supplied to both conditions for each pair, the unique n10 discordant episode must be attributable to either (a) a guarded-emulation observation that the validator did not flag, or (b) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The archived execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts link the recorded repair event to a single pair_id; auditors can locate that pair in the canonical bundle to inspect the validator_trace and repair transcript for attribution. We do not reproduce raw logs here; the canonical execution manifesto and artifact bundle contains the full per-episode traces for verification.

Representative diagnostics. Representative scoring traces for sampled episodes show validator_trace fields with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for the overwhelming majority of items, consistent with the observed baseline ceiling effect. Emulation observations largely corroborated validator outcomes across the curated task bank; the single guarded-only detection corresponds to the single registered repair-stage event under the run accounting described above.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation. The near-zero aggregate marginal benefit of sandboxed emulation in this regime is explained by three artifact-supported factors: (1) validator ceiling effect—deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes the workflow patterns exercised by the curated task bank, leaving little headroom for additional detections; (2) curated inclusion rules—confirmatory items required parser acceptance and were drawn from a deterministic generator that constrained input diversity and adversarial exposure; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics and minimal repair activity—the only downstream events able to create discordance are emulation observations or the single documented repair invocation (provider-call audit shows repair = 1). These factors are documented in the archived execution and analysis artifacts and delimit the interpretive scope of the finding.

Operational implications. For operator pipelines that enforce strong parser validation and maintain a validator whose rule set closely matches expected intent patterns, the marginal detection yield from an always-on automated sandboxed-emulation stage may be small and operationally costly. Conversely, in settings characterized by noisy natural-language intents, adversarial misconfiguration attempts, larger vendor diversity, or longer-lived stateful interactions, guarded sandboxing is likely to surface runtime semantics and side-effects that static validators cannot anticipate, and thus its marginal value may be greater. Practical deployment should therefore consider selective/targeted sandboxing for high‑risk changes or use adversarial test banks to identify validator gaps.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting indicates a single repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping. We interpret this near-zero finding as a narrow, artifact-supported consequence of validator ceiling effects and curated input selection. Broader generalization requires retesting on adversarial, multi‑vendor, and higher‑fidelity emulation regimes. The archived execution and analysis artifacts provide reproducible seeds for such extensions.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
